Company organized around four themes: category disruption (Celsius + Alani drove 50% of 2024 US energy growth), a large/growing functional-beverage TAM, a 'more people, more places, more often' growth strategy, and strong cash generation deployed through disciplined capital allocation.
Positioned as the #3 US energy portfolio at 16.6% tracked-channel share - closer to #2 Monster than to the #4 brand below; $3.5B 2024 retail sales, ~$2B 2024 pro forma net revenue.

Celsius was a 'rocket ship' with triple-digit growth ~2020-2024, hit 'a little bit of a slow period last year,' and has maintained ~11% market share over the trailing nine months - framed as a strong foundation to re-accelerate from, not a decline.
Celsius brand ACV 98.7% across 241,000+ outlets; Alani Nu ACV in the low-80s with significant upside; Celsius Holdings has picked up ~10 share points of energy MULO+ since Q1 2022.

Alani Nu's lower gross margin (~8-10 points below Celsius) attributed firmly to scale, not mix - shared ingredients, same can suppliers, same manufacturing facilities; buying power moving from $1.5B to $2-plus billion should enhance margins.

Management pushed back on the crossover/cannibalization view - only ~1-2% of Alani Nu followers also follow Celsius; the brands serve highly differentiated consumers (Celsius 50-50 male/female, Alani Nu 90%+ female, younger 18-24); Alani is incremental, not cannibalistic.

First-ever Celsius limited-time offering planned for Q3/Q4 2025 - an excellent way to drive consumption frequency within the existing base; LTOs (Monster, Red Bull, Alani Nu) have driven a lot of category growth.
Newly announced 'Live Fit Go' comprehensive 360-degree marketing campaign (digital, TV, social) broadens the Celsius message beyond gym users to mainstream consumers.

Core Celsius distribution up 15-20% in 2025 (CEO-cited target), the bulk already on shelf from January-May resets, a couple of large retailers still to come; summer innovation (a couple of SKUs) and the later-year LTO bring additional placements.
Alani Nu's 2025 distribution gains described as 'substantial' (not publicly detailed), with further distribution upside through the rest of 2025 and into 2026.

Alani Nu distribution decision (ABI vs. Pepsi) remains open - 'we haven't made any decisions yet and there's really nothing to talk about publicly'; the company values optionality between Pepsi and the fragmented AB Independent Beer Network, where Alani gets significant attention.
24-month Alani Nu integration toward a Celsius-like margin profile (Alani ~2-3 years behind Celsius), rolling Alani into Celsius's supplier contracts and scaling buying power.

Big Beverage (North Carolina contract manufacturer, acquired November 2024) could eventually handle ~20% of total Celsius/Alani production, serving most of the Southeast - one line in place with infrastructure for a second; in-house production is margin-friendly.
Q1 2025 gross margin 52%; combined 2024 pro forma gross margin ~48%; some vertical-integration benefit started to be seen in Q1.

Capital allocation disciplined - net leverage ~1.0x with ample cash, goal of reducing leverage over time; fuel organic growth, invest in innovation/marketing, maintain a strong balance sheet and pay down debt; cash-EPS accretive in year one; opportunistic M&A with Alani Nu integration as the explicit #1 priority.

Category evolved from a niche, male-dominated, young thrill-seeker category 20 years ago to mainstream, gender-balanced, age-balanced, lifestyle/functional-focused; sugar-free overtook full sugar for the first time last year (>50%).
A report cited that women are driving energy drink growth right now - the Celsius/Alani Nu portfolio is positioned to capitalize; energy/CSD lines are blurring.

Consumer bounced back - convenience-channel foot traffic improved (lower gas prices); last year's slowdown attributed mainly to macro issues; category grew ~7% in Q1 2025, accelerated in the trailing four weeks.

Exploring an Alani Nu-style 100-milligram-caffeine smaller can for core Celsius; suggested 'fewer but bigger' innovation and more focused national campaigns, plus 'true innovation' vs. flavor innovation, going forward.

Incremental marketing spend - 'probably a little bit of additional spend' behind Live Fit Go (S&M % addressed at the Celsius Holdings level on the modeling call); the two big players (especially Red Bull) spend heavily on marketing.
Dublin center of excellence (set up 2024) supports innovation, global procurement, supply chain and global marketing; the company is investing in AI-assisted tools to drive sales and efficiency.
Reported net revenue diverges from Circana/Nielsen scanner data during a growth phase due to order ebbs and flows - the modeling call's five-quarter view was provided for that perspective.
What Celsius is seeing more recently in the energy category after last year's slowdown, and expectations for 2025.

The consumer bounced back with improved convenience-channel foot traffic (lower gas prices), benefiting Celsius given its convenience skew. Red Bull leaning into sugar-free and LTOs has driven category growth, as have Monster and Alani Nu LTOs; Celsius launches its first LTO in Q3/Q4 to drive frequency. Last year's slowdown was mainly macro. The category grew ~7% in Q1 2025 and accelerated in the trailing four weeks.
Whether the 15-20% distribution gain is Celsius, Alani Nu, or both, and when those gains hit shelves.

The 15-20% reference is for core Celsius (a CEO-cited target), gains pretty much all on shelf after January-May resets, a couple of large retailers still to come. Summer innovation (a couple of SKUs) and the later-year LTO bring additional placements. Alani Nu's 2025 distribution gains were 'substantial,' not publicly detailed, with further upside for the rest of 2025 and into 2026.
Whether Alani Nu would become part of the Pepsi distribution system.

Not commenting publicly; the company values the optionality between Pepsi and the fragmented AB Independent Beer Network (which has lost key brands over the last 2-3 years, so Alani Nu gets significant attention there). Pros for both networks, but no decision made and nothing to discuss publicly.
Given the effort to broaden Celsius beyond the gym user, whether the company will spend more on marketing and is leaning in enough.

The modeling call addressed the S&M percentage for the rest of the year at the Celsius Holdings level (including Alani Nu); anticipates a little bit of additional spend going into the Live Fit Go initiative. The two big players (especially Red Bull) are spending heavily on marketing, making it important for Celsius to lean into the campaign.
Alani Nu Margin Gap (Mix vs. Scale)
Whether Alani Nu's margins (~8-10 points below Celsius) reflect its non-energy mix or simply scale.

Just scale - Alani Nu is where Celsius was 2-3 years ago at a similar size. The brands share many ingredients, source cans from the same three big players, use many of the same manufacturing facilities. Rolling Alani Nu into Celsius's contracts plus the scale benefit (buying power from $1.5B to $2-plus billion) should enhance margins; no reason Alani Nu cannot reach a Celsius-like margin profile - hopefully faster than the 24 months cited.
Whether a lower-caffeine version or smaller hand size is being considered to support a broader customer base.

Alani Nu already has a smaller 100-milligram-caffeine can, which Celsius is exploring for its core brand. The innovation team evaluates many opportunities; agreed Celsius has done a lot of flavor assortment and suggested 'fewer but bigger,' more focused national campaigns, and 'true innovation' versus flavor innovation could be opportunities going forward.
Whether the ~20% production figure for Big Beverage applies to Celsius volume only or includes Alani Nu.

It applies to both Celsius and Alani Nu. The plant currently has one line with infrastructure to add a second; North Carolina is a major US beverage manufacturing hub with nearby co-packers and good freight lanes to serve the Southeast. A huge opportunity, and in-house production is margin-friendly.
When the benefits of the vertical integration would be realized (question heavily affected by technical difficulty).
Maybe a little bit in Q1 / Q4 - not necessarily - but some of the benefit started to be seen in Q1.
